command.mac: Read-only check, change nothing. Part 1, in Bash: echo "id=$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"; ls -l ~/.claude/settings.json; grep -n defaultMode ~/.claude/settings.json || echo 'no defaultMode'; echo "CS_SESSION_ROLE=$CS_SESSION_ROLE". Then tell me which permission mode this session is in right now (the mode indicator under the input box). Part 2, in this claude-settings clone: run ls -t ~/.claude/projects/*/ | head -5. Then find the newest session log that contains a start_session tool call (grep -l start_session over the newest 20 logs under ~/.claude/projects) and print the 3 lines around the first permission prompt or 'asked' record for it. File names only, no secrets. Report, nothing else: the four outputs of part 1, the mode, whether that start asked for a confirm (yes or no), and the tool name it used (mcp__ccd_session__start_session or another).
